title: Deleted from India's voter rolls, some Muslims face detention, deportation
authors: Sarita Chaganti Singh, Mohammad Ponir Hossain (Reuters)
shows: Reuters reports that India's revision of the rolls left off or deleted 130 million names, and it says data shows the omissions fall disproportionately on Muslims. It spoke to 10 families whose relatives were detained, deported or questioned about their citizenship after their names were dropped from the rolls, and it says all of them had Indian identity or family documents while relatives, among them parents and siblings, stayed on the rolls. It reports that a woman from West Bengal, on the state's rolls since at least 2008 by the voter card Reuters saw, says she was detained in Mumbai on 19 July and forced across the border into Bangladesh, and that court filings show she was one of 149 people deported in that operation. It reports that Mumbai's Foreigners Regional Registration Office told the Calcutta High Court she had produced a Bangladeshi birth certificate and no valid or credible documentary evidence of Indian citizenship, and that she disputes this. It reports a petition in the Calcutta High Court by five people who say they were detained after their names were deleted from the rolls while their appeals were pending before the special tribunals. One of them told Reuters that police in Chhattisgarh detained him with 22 others, that 19 were released after 14 days when their names were found on the revised rolls, and that he and three others were held for 32 days. It cites the Sabar Institute for the finding that Muslims were about 70% of the 2.7 million names deleted in West Bengal after a closer review, against 27% of the population. It quotes Home Minister Amit Shah at a rally in Haryana on 5 November saying that the BJP would detect infiltrators, remove them from the rolls and expel them. It says that removal from the roll does not by itself establish that anyone is a foreigner, and that the Home Ministry, the Prime Minister's Office and the Election Commission did not respond to a request for comment.
quote: The cases show how India’s sweeping voter-roll revision has become entangled with a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner.
Muslims made up about 70% of the 2.7 million names deleted after a closer review, despite being 27% of the population, according to the Kolkata-based Sabar Institute.
note: First reading, 16 November 2026. Reuters copy, datelined Swarupnagar and Satkhira, 16 November, by Sarita Chaganti Singh and Mohammad Ponir Hossain, with additional reporting by Jatindra Dash, writing by Aftab Ahmed and editing by Saad Sayeed, as carried by ThePrint (published 2026-11-16T02:30:03+00:00, marked as auto-generated from the Reuters feed and (c) Thomson Reuters 2026). Read in full from ThePrint's page with curl on 16 November 2026. The Reuters original could not be read: reuters.com answered curl with 401, and no other free copy was sought. Linked through ThePrint, as round 34 linked PTI copy through ThePrint. The story names several private people, a woman deported, her husband, a hawker who petitioned the High Court and a neighbour of the Murshidabad holding centre, and none of them is named here. The Sabar Institute's founder and a human rights activist it quotes are not carried. Every claim on religion, detention, deportation and citizenship is Reuters' or that of the filings and people it cites. The 130 million agrees with the site's count of 13,39,03,307 names left off the drafts in 31 states (data/india/states.json, total). The 9 million names Reuters says West Bengal cut and the Sabar Institute's 2.7 million deleted after a closer review are not figures the site holds. The site has 58,20,899 left off West Bengal's draft, 5,46,053 deleted after it and 60,06,675 withheld for adjudication, and it does not hold how many of those withheld were deleted. Reuters' description of the BJP and its opening framing are not carried, and the summary keeps to what the story reports.

title: Special Summary Revision: About 50 lakh voters added across 9 states; fraction of SIR removals
shows: Hindustan Times sets the draft rolls of the special summary revision, published on 12 November, against the final rolls of the intensive revision and reports about 50 lakh electors added across the nine states and union territories for which figures were released, with rises of 0.1% to 3%. It gives Bihar about 7.55 crore electors, about 13 lakh more than its final roll of 7.42 crore. It gives Tamil Nadu about 5.77 crore, about 10 lakh more than its final roll and below the 6.41 crore it held before the intensive revision. It gives Madhya Pradesh 8.19 lakh more for nearly 5.48 crore, Rajasthan a rise of 2.22% or about 11 lakh, and Kerala 2.736 crore against 2.695 crore, about 4.06 lakh more. It puts the largest rise in Goa, about 3%, with about 43,000 names added and at least 11,000 deleted. It gives Uttarakhand 1,25,216 names added and 6,130 applications for deletion processed, and Manipur about 33,700 more. It sets the additions beside the fall in the rolls from about 50.9 crore to 44.4 crore at the drafts of the intensive revision's second phase in 12 states and union territories, and it says applicants in the summary revision do not have to submit documents proving citizenship or be mapped to earlier rolls. It reports that Uttar Pradesh moved its draft to 17 November, that claims and objections close on 11 December and that the final rolls are due on 4 January.
quote: Goa recorded the steepest rise at 3%, followed by Rajasthan at 2.22%. In Goa, about 43,000 voters were added. At least 11,000 names were deleted.
The addition of about five million (50 lakh) across the nine states is a fraction of the voters removed under SIR.
note: First reading, 16 November 2026. Read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 16 November 2026, which marks it isAccessibleForFree true. Byline Himanshi Dahiya, datePublished 2026-11-16T10:52:47+05:30, modified 11:17:40. HT gives its figures in millions, and the summary gives them in crore and lakh. Checked against data/india/raw/ssr_draft.csv and final.csv. Madhya Pradesh agrees exactly (8,18,563 more, 5,47,99,628). Kerala agrees (2,73,60,254 against 2,69,53,644, 4,06,610 more). Manipur agrees (19,94,357 against 19,60,620, 33,737 more). Rajasthan's 2.22% agrees (5,26,67,416 against 5,15,19,929, 11,47,487 or 2.23%), and HT's 'about 52 million' is low for 5.27 crore. Tamil Nadu agrees (5,77,46,618 against 5,67,07,380, 10,39,238 more, and 6,41,14,587 before the revision in states.json). Bihar's rise is 13,97,008 in the file against the final roll of 30 September 2025, which HT gives as about 1.3 million where it rounds to 1.4. Uttarakhand's 1,25,216 additions agree, and the file does not hold the 6,130 applications for deletion, and HT's draft of 7.27 million is 72,78,035 in the file, or 7.28. Goa has no row in ssr_draft.csv because no count of its draft has been found. HT's 43,000 added and at least 11,000 deleted would give a net rise of about 32,000, which is 3.0% of Goa's final roll of 10,57,566, so the 3% is consistent with them. HT says data was unavailable for Assam, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Punjab, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The file has drafts for Assam and Chhattisgarh from press reports, HT gives Uttarakhand's figures itself, and in process.json the drafts of Gujarat, West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands fall after 12 November. HT says drafts were published in 13 states and three union territories on 12 November, and process.json now schedules 13 drafts for that day, with those of Uttar Pradesh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands on 17 November. The rise of 0.1% to 3% fits Lakshadweep's 0.16% at the low end. The rises in the file for the nine (Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Kerala, Manipur, Puducherry and Lakshadweep, with Goa's 32,000) add to 48,87,523, close to 50 lakh. The second-phase fall from 50.9 crore to 44.4 crore agrees with the 6,56,77,447 left off in 12 states in states.json (by_phase). HT's figure of 20.5 million or 13.27% deleted in the final rolls does not match a figure the site holds and is not carried. HT's opening line says 'tens of thousands' were removed in the intensive revision, which is a slip for tens of millions and is not carried. Its account of the Election Commissioners' disagreement over the summary revision, the Economic Times report, and its last paragraph on West Bengal's result are not carried.
